newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Euro-Mediterranean businessmen meet in Morocco.
newsitem.headline: Euro-Mediterranean businessmen meet in Morocco.

text.p: More than 400 businessmen from 25 European and Mediterranean countries on Thursday started discussions on boosting cooperation between private enterprises of the two sides of the Mediterranean.

"We should set up a constructive mutual partnership for a common space of cooperation, peace and prosperity between the two banks of the Mediterranean," Driss Jettou, Moroccan Trade Minister, told the opening ceremony.
Held in the red-walled tourist city of Marrakesh, the meeting aims at "reducing differences and tensions between countries of the region", Jettou said.

Described as the second Euro-Mediterranean summit of businessmen, the meeting plans to establish the first signposts to bring to reality "the bilateral and multilateral commitment of the Mediterranean countries by the year 2010", one Moroccan businessman said.
The previous meeting took place in Valencia, Spain, last year, an official said.

"The Marrakesh meeting will evaluate the level of cooperation between Euro-Mediterranean countries in the light of continued political and economic changes," Ahmed Benkirane, vice president of the Moroccan Businessmen's Confederation told Reuters.
"We will also present concrete proposals to consolidate economic cooperation between the private sector in the whole region."

Israel and Syria and Lebanon were originally expected to attend the meeting but had turned down the invitation. Syria earlier said it would not attend a meeting in an Arab country if Israel was invited too, an official said.
Libya, which is a member of the North African Arab Maghreb Union, was not present at the meeting, the official said but gave no details.

After the opening ceremony, delegations were to hold separate meetings in workshops dealing with North-South cooperation, instruments of financial cooperation, the fisheries industry, tourism, infrastructure, environment and energy, and new technology.
Among other countries invited to the Marrakesh meeting are Russia, Switzerland, Mauritania, Norway, Poland,and Hungary.
